@albertosantini Thanks for the issue! If you're reporting a bug, please be sure to include:
1. The version of ESLint you are using (run `eslint -v`)
2. What you did (the source code and ESLint configuration)
3. The actual ESLint output complete with numbers
4. What you expected to happen instead

Requesting a new rule? Please see [Proposing a New Rule](http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules) for instructions.

Thank you for this issue.

I can reproduce this.
mmm, `eslint@2.0.0-beta.3` and later seem to be searching in local installed configs even if the eslint was installed to global.

@nzakas Is this intentional behavior?

Yes, this is intentional. We changed it so we search for shareable configs relative to the config file that references it. http://eslint.org/blog/2016/02/eslint-v2.0.0-rc.0-released#shareable-config-changes

I think the question note is if we want to add back an exception for global install or not? Iirc, fixing people to install shareable configs globally was a point of confusion.

I read that note and it should not be valid for a global setup.
At least, I didn't understand it would be applied also for the global setup.

If `eslint` is installed globally, at the moment with `rc.0`, I would be compelled to create a complete config file without `extends` field to lint casual files (out of a project).

It would be not an issue for the "projects", because `eslint` and `eslint-config-eslint` are installed locally. But for the rest of the cases? For the folders containing snippets?

Surely I am missing something here.

To fix my use case should I add to my `local` config something like `"extends": "C:\\Users\\icebox\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\node_modules\\eslint-config-eslint\\default.yml"`?

(Tested and it works, but ugly, I think)

I need to update the description for sure. To be honest, I didn't realize it would affect the global setup as I forgot that globally installed modules weren't in the hierarchy from the current working directory.

Making this change not apply in the case of a global install isn't easy - there's no real indication as to whether ESLint is running from a global install or a local install. 

So yes, in the meantime you can directly add a full path in `extends`.
@nzakas With this change, configs/plugins are resolved based on the path of the .eslintrc file, right? What happens when a user only have config file in the user directory?
@ilyavolodin `extends` and `plugins` are calculated relative to that file as well.

issue.body:
With 2.0.0-rc.0, the `extends` and `plugins` fields of config files are resolved relative to the config file itself. This can cause issues when, for example, the home directory config file is used (`~/.eslintrc`). In that case, the resolution for `extends` and `plugins` would begin in the home directory rather than in the project directory, meaning that the shareable config or plugin won't be found. As a concrete example:
1. The project is in `~/projects/foo`
2. The project has no local `.eslintrc` file
3. There is a `~/.eslintrc` file that references `eslint-config-bar`
4. The `eslint-config-bar` package is installed in `~/projects/foo/node_modules/eslint-config-bar`

In this example, ESLint will not find `eslint-config-bar` because the search for that module will begin in `~/node_modules` because that's relative to the config file.
## Possible Solutions
1. If the config file path is a descendant of the CWD, use the config file path.
2. If the CWD is a descendant of the config file path, use the CWD.
3. If the config file path and CWD are not in the same hierarchy, just use the default behavior of `require`.

body:
`plugins` and `extends` seem to be difference on `rc.0`.
`extends` is calculated relative to `.eslintrc`, but `plugins` seem to be not.

```
echo plugins: ["node"] > .eslintrc.yml
echo console.log("hello") > test.js
npm i -g eslint@next
npm i eslint-plugin-node
eslint test.js
```

```
C:\Users\t-nagashima.AD\nodist\bin\node_modules\eslint\lib\config\plugins.js:120
                throw err;
                ^

Error: Failed to load plugin node: Cannot find module 'eslint-plugin-node'
    at Function.Module._resolveFilename (module.js:337:15)
    at Function.Module._load (module.js:287:25)
    at Module.require (module.js:366:17)
    at require (module.js:385:17)
    at Object.module.exports.load (C:\Users\t-nagashima.AD\nodist\bin\node_modules\eslint\lib\config\plugins.js:116:26)
    at Array.forEach (native)
    at Object.module.exports.loadAll (C:\Users\t-nagashima.AD\nodist\bin\node_modules\eslint\lib\config\plugins.js:134:21)
    at Object.load (C:\Users\t-nagashima.AD\nodist\bin\node_modules\eslint\lib\config\config-file.js:419:21)
    at loadConfig (C:\Users\t-nagashima.AD\nodist\bin\node_modules\eslint\lib\config.js:67:33)
    at getLocalConfig (C:\Users\t-nagashima.AD\nodist\bin\node_modules\eslint\lib\config.js:129:23)
```
@mysticatea you're correct, I mistyped. `plugins` work the same as always, its `extends` and `parser` that are resolved from the config file.

This is breaking tools such as [Canonical](https://github.com/gajus/canonical) and [Standard](https://github.com/feross/standard).

A program has its own [`eslintrc.json`](https://github.com/gajus/canonical/blob/v3.0.3/src/syntaxes/js/eslintrc.json). That it then uses to [lint text using CLIEngine](https://github.com/gajus/canonical/blob/v3.0.3/src/syntaxes/js/lintText.js#L7-L18). When attempting to run the program against an arbitrary code base, I get:

> Cannot find module 'eslint-config-canonical-lodash' from '/Users/gajus/Documents/dev/gajus/react-outside-event'

What I expect is for CLIEngine to resolve this plugin against Canonical module, since it is Canonical that is running the `CLIEngine`. However, it appears that `CLIEngine` is picking up the current working directory and therefore cannot resolve the configs.
